pages.text: "I'm a white mouse!" Coco bounced on a flour sack. Flour covered Coco from head to tail. Only the headscarf was red; everything else was white. Mr. Pig, who carried flour sacks, chuckled.
"Coco, I've filled the wooden tub. Time to wash!" Mom called from behind the kitchen. "No! I want to go around the alley as a white mouse!" Coco hid behind the sack.
But the summer sun was hot, and drops of sweat appeared. The flour mixed with sweat and stuck to Coco's back. "Huh? Why am I so itchy?" Coco scratched their back.
Mom crouched in front of Coco. "Instead of washing, shall we play at making clouds?" "Clouds? How?" Mom held out her front paw.
Water rippled in the big wooden tub behind the kitchen. Coco dipped one floury paw in. White flour drifted into the water, billowing like a cloud. "Wow! A cloud!"
"Our cloud game has an order," Mom whispered. "Headscarf on the peg, splash into a big cloud, a soap snowman, then rinse!" Coco took off the scarf and hung it on the peg. "Wash off the flour—splash!"
Splash! Coco jumped in. A big flour cloud spread over the water. Mom rubbed with bubbly soap, and Coco became a white foam snowman. Mr. Pig clapped. Wash off the flour—splash!
After rinsing off the bubbles, Coco came out fresh and dry. All the stickiness was gone. "Washing feels this cool?" Mom put the headscarf back on, and Coco straightened their shoulders.
The next day, Coco ran to the tub first. "Let's play clouds again! One, headscarf on the peg! Two, splash into a big cloud! Three, a bubble snowman, then rinse!" Coco didn't miss a single step.
Mom sat down and hugged clean, dry Coco in both arms. Wash away the flour, and clouds float on the water while your body feels lighter. Coco called from Mom's arms, "Wash off the flour—splash!"
